summary: The 3 build errors in modalExpandBranches_closed_unsat's succ-case `key` fuel-induction cannot be closed by a local repair. Genuine effort (relax/drop the vestigial hstep premise, inline modalStepBranch_preserves_sat, reformulate `key` with per-branch freshness) reduces the proof to three obligations on the post-step shared accumulator. Two of them are MATHEMATICALLY FALSE for carried sibling branches: the freshness invariant and the satisfiability needed for the contradiction. A build-verified Lean counterexample is included. Root cause is the shared-`acc` + per-branch fresh-world (modalNextWorld) design, which lets a diamond rule in one branch pollute sibling branches in the worklist. This is a real soundness-proof hole beyond drift; closing it needs a definitional change (out of scope), not a 3-error fix.

blockers.what_was_done: Relaxed then DROPPED the vestigial hstep hypothesis (its `b in branches` premise was unprovable and the hypothesis itself is unthreadable: it is tied to a fixed `acc` while the recursion changes `acc` to `newAcc`). Replaced it by inlining modalStepBranch_preserves_sat, which is universally quantified over acc. Reformulated `key` to carry per-branch freshness `(hpInv : forall bp in pending, accFreshInv bp acc)`. This reduces the entire succ-case to THREE helper obligations on the new worklist `done ++ newBs ++ bt` at `newAcc` -- build-confirmed: after the reformulation the only remaining errors were the four references to these three helpers.
blockers.obligation_1_maintenance_newBs: accFreshInv b' newAcc for every result branch b' in newBs. TRUE and provable (each newBs branch contains b plus, in fresh-world rules, a witness at label modalNextWorld b, so modalNextWorld b' > the new edge target).
blockers.obligation_2_freshness_carried_FALSE: accFreshInv bp acc -> accFreshInv bp newAcc for a carried sibling branch bp. FALSE: modalApplyOne (diamondPos/boxNeg) adds edge (w, w') with w' = modalNextWorld b (PER-BRANCH numbering for the expanded branch b). A sibling bp produced by an earlier propositional `.branching` shares b's labels, so modalNextWorld bp = modalNextWorld b = w'. accFreshInv bp newAcc requires the new edge target w' < modalNextWorld bp, i.e. w' < w' -- false (strict inequality).
blockers.obligation_3_sat_carried_FALSE_build_ver: branchSatisfiable bp acc -> branchSatisfiable bp newAcc for a carried branch bp. FALSE, verified by a compiling Lean `example`: bp = [T(box p)@0, T(box (p -> bot))@0] is satisfiable at Accessibility.empty (dead-end world 0 makes both boxes vacuous) but NOT satisfiable after empty.addEdge 0 1 (world 0 gains successor 1, forcing p and not-p at world 1).
blockers.root_cause: modalExpandBranches threads a SINGLE shared `acc` through all worklist branches, while modalApplyOne numbers fresh worlds PER-BRANCH via modalNextWorld. An edge created by one branch's existential (diamond/boxNeg) rule is therefore visible to and constrains sibling branches that do not contain that fresh world. modalStepBranch_preserves_sat REQUIRES per-branch accFreshInv of the expanded branch for its fresh-world witness construction; this precondition is false for any branch processed after a sibling created a fresh world. The maintainable flatMap-level invariant accFreshInv (flatMap branches) acc is strictly WEAKER and cannot supply the per-branch accFreshInv that preserves_sat (and the hstep call at 1749) demand.
blockers.verbatim_obligation_at_1749: freshness arg requires `accFreshInv bp acc` for the branch being expanded; the only invariant maintainable through the recursion is the strictly weaker flatMap-level `accFreshInv (branches.flatMap id) acc`, from which the per-branch fact does not follow (wrong direction: modalNextWorld bp <= modalNextWorld (flatMap branches)).
blockers.what_is_needed: One of (none is a local 3-error repair; all require revisiting the recognizer/expansion DEFINITIONS, which the task scope forbids): (A) give each branch its OWN accessibility relation so fresh worlds/edges are branch-local (changes modalStepBranch / modalExpandBranches signatures and behavior); (B) thread a globally-monotone fresh-world counter so fresh indices never collide across branches; (C) prove a much stronger GLOBAL invariant coupling box-positive consistency across all worklist branches so the cross-branch pollution is provably harmless (major proof redesign).

continuation_context.resume_at: modalExpandBranches_closed_unsat succ-case; but DO NOT retry as a local proof repair -- requires a design decision (per-branch acc OR global fresh-world counter) from the maintainer first.
continuation_context.recommended_next_action: Escalate the design question: should modalExpandBranches give each branch its own Accessibility, or use a global fresh-world counter? Either resolves the cross-branch pollution. Then re-plan the soundness proof against the revised definitions.
